title: kernel-topology-occupancy-mapper-nsight-snapshots-2026-03
content:
Context and goal:
- We see intermittent tail latency spikes on medium-size models (8-12k context) during mixed small/large batch workloads. Hypothesis: topology of kernel launches + CUDA graph stitching combined with host copy phasing is causing transient occupancy collapse on SMs (short windows where many SMs idle).

High-level summary (tl;dr):
- Replayed several Nsight captures with fine-grain NVTX markers around batch handoff. Found recurring pattern: a group of persistent decoder kernels that should fuse are split across two CUDA graph segments after runtime-level graph stitching. The split introduces a small gap where L2 prefetches happen but many SMs are descheduled, causing occupancy drop from ~92% -> ~24% for 1-3ms per request. This aligns with tail latency windows.

What I ran (quick log):
- Repro recipe: model: open-7b-encoder-decoder variant, sequence len 10/4096 mix, microbatching enabled with pipeline depth 2.
- Nsight Systems captures: nsight --session decode-topology-2026-03 --capture-range nvtx --trace cuda,cudnn,osrt --output decode-topology-2026-03.nsys-rep
- Sample capture IDs: S001 (2026-03-12 14:05), S002 (2026-03-14 09:40), S003 (2026-03-16 11:22)
- Filtering: used nvprof-style grouping via NVTX markers from runtime: "BATCH_START", "KERNEL_FUSE_POINT", "CUDAGRAPH_BEGIN", "CUDAGRAPH_END", "HOST_COPY_HOLD"

Observations (raw):
- Timeline slice (representative S002):
  * 0.0ms: BATCH_START host prefetch
  * 1.2ms: CUDAGRAPH_BEGIN (graph A) -> includes attention+ffn kernels for steps 1-6
  * 4.8ms: CUDAGRAPH_END (graph A) -> immediate host memcpy queued
  * 5.1ms: small host->device copy (20KB) with high PCIe latency (avg 0.9ms)
  * 5.9ms: CUDAGRAPH_BEGIN (graph B) -> remaining decoder kernels 7-12
  * 6.3ms: observed per-SM active occupancy drop (from 92% to 24%) for 0.9ms window
  * 7.2ms: occupancy recovered, graph B finishes at 8.1ms
- SM waveform shows a clumping pattern: many warps launch but stall waiting for L2 misses amplified during the small memcpy window. The prefetch window appears to thrash L2 and sharedmem banks for a brief period.

Micro-metrics (extracted from Nsight counters):
- avg_warp_execution_efficiency: 0.67 -> dips to 0.28 in the 5.9-7.0ms window
- achieved_occupancy: 0.92 -> 0.24 (per-SM sampled)
- l2_read_requests: +220% during memcpy window compared to baseline slice
- shared_memory_bank_conflicts: small increase (~12%) on certain kernels (ffn-custom)

Hypothesis refinement:
- The runtime’s CUDA graph stitching currently carves graphs at host-copy boundaries (safe) but sometimes the kernel fusion boundary is misaligned with the graph boundary (kernel topology dependent e.g., when a multi-kernel fusion would be beneficial). When stitching is done naively the small host copy runs between two fusion-equivalent kernels causing temporary resource imbalance: some kernels prefetch or prime caches while others are descheduled -> net occupancy loss.

Why this matters:
- Even though the gap is small (sub-ms to a few ms), it maps to the observed 99.9th percentile tail spikes because concurrent requests can coincide with these windows. For low-latency SLAs that we promise on dedicated capacity, this is material.

Quick experiments tried:
1) Force single-graph replay: pinned both halves into one CUDA graph (workaround) -> tail spikes disappear in replay, occupancy held ~88-94%. But single-graph increases peak memory temp by ~3% and complicates incremental update/rollout logic.
2) Insert a small stream-synchronization pacer (sleep 50us) between host copy and second graph -> reduced L2 thrash but increased median latency slightly. Still a useful diagnostic prove-of-concept.
3) Align prefetch windows: moved routine that issues L2 warmup from before memcpy to immediately after graph B begin -> reduced L2 spike but difficult to maintain correctness for some models.

Additional evidence (counterfactuals):
- When we disable microbatch pipeline (single microbatch), the pattern shifts but the occupancy dip persists at slightly different offsets -> indicates root cause is graph boundary + host copy, not microbatch logic alone.
- Changing PCIe gen (test infra with PCIe4 -> PCIe5) reduced host-copy latency and amplitude of L2 thrash, but didn't eliminate the case entirely on heavy-attention heads.

Open questions:
- Are there kernel-level prefetch heuristics we can adapt so that kernels that will run across a graph boundary perform less aggressive L2 prefetch when a host copy is pending?
- Can the graph stitching policy include a topology-aware decision: if two kernels are fusion-candidates and the host-copy window is below some threshold, attempt to preserve them in the same graph?
- How brittle is the single-graph workaround across models with larger context or different attention patterns?

Suggested next actions (short term -> long term):
- Short term (1-2 weeks):
  * Implement an experimental topology-aware grapher flag (rt.experimental.topology_preserve = true) which biases the graph cut scoring to avoid breaks where fusion score > X. Add unit tests and fuzzing. (Owner: Evan)
  * Add a light-weight NVTX sampling probe in runtime to measure real-time per-GPU occupancy slides and log to console for Canary deployments. (Owner: Li)
  * Add CI replay that runs the single-graph vs stitched graphs on a subset of models and records occupancy delta. (Owner: Priya)
- Mid term (3-6 weeks):
  * Evaluate kernel prefetch heuristic adjustments with applied microbenchmarks (Marta).
  * Explore predictive host-copy batching to reduce number of small memcpy windows (platform infra).
- Long term (quarter):
  * Consider adaptive graph compilation that can recompile on-the-fly to fuse sequences if runtime telemetry shows repeated occupancy loss events.

Notes / runbook snippets (for engineers reproducing):
- To reproduce with a lightweight harness: set RWI_MICROBATCH_DEPTH=2 RWI_ENABLE_CUDAGRAPH_STITCH=1 RWI_TOPOLOGY_SCORE=0.3 and use the model test harness in experiments/replay/kernel-topology-harness
- Nsight capture tips:
  * Add NVTX ranges around runtime graph compile and submission to make post-filters easy.
  * Use SASS-level sampler for warp efficiency; collect L2 counters and sharedmem bank counters.

Relevant tickets and artifacts:
- INF-7863: intermittent tail-latency investigation (parent)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/842 (patch with nvtx probes)
- Confluence: kernel-topology-matrix (design notes)

Appendix (quick mental model diagrams in text):
- Good case: [K1+K2 fused inside GraphA] -> launches saturate SMs -> high occupancy
- Bad case: [K1 in GraphA] -> host copy -> [K2 in GraphB] -> K1 finishes, small host copy starts, K2 launches but many warps delayed until prefetch finishes -> occupancy trough

Action items assigned (short):
- Evan: spike topology_preserve grapher + simple scoring (due 2026-03-25)
- Li: runtime NVTX occupancy logger + canary hook (due 2026-03-22)
- Marta: microbenchmark that exercises L2 prefetch variance (due 2026-04-05)
- Priya: add CI comparison job + aggregate replay metrics into perf dashboard (due 2026-03-29)

Notes-to-self (misc):
- Keep captures S001/S002/S003; make sure to tag with full env metadata (driver, cuda, nvidia-smi).
- Try to capture on a machine with ECC off and on to rule out small timing differences from error-correction paths.

End of doc.
